concept.name: Low-volume node
concept.definition: A valley in the volume profile — a price zone where traded volume was significantly lower than in neighboring zones, typically because price moved through it quickly during a breakout or breakdown. LVNs mark prices the market did not accept, and price tends either to traverse them quickly again or to bounce off their edges.
concept.intuition: An LVN is a stretch of road the market drove through without stopping — few transactions ever cleared there.
concept.mechanics: Read from the volume-at-price histogram as local minima (thin sections) between high-volume nodes; they often separate distributions and coincide with single-print zones on TPO profiles.
concept.failure_modes: LVNs fill in as later sessions trade through them, after which the 'rejection zone' logic no longer applies; like HVNs, their boundaries depend on row-size settings.
concept.misconceptions: An LVN is not a gap that must be filled, nor a guaranteed fast-move zone on every revisit — once business is done there, the informational content decays.
concept.example: Between two profile bulges sits a thin zone at 4,510–4,514; when price re-enters it the next session, it traverses the band in two bars and consolidates at the far edge.
